question: According to Huygens' principle, each point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets. However, we only observe a wave propagating forward. How is the absence of a backward propagating wave explained in the modified wave theory?

options.A: By the destructive interference of secondary wavelets in the backward direction
options.B: By assuming the intensity of secondary wavelets varies as $(1 + \cos \theta)$, which becomes zero for $\theta = \pi$
options.C: By the conservation of energy principle which forbids backward flow
options.D: By the fact that light particles (corpuscles) have forward momentum only
